payingUser: A print-on-demand, merch or digital-download seller on Etsy, eBay, Depop, Vinted, Amazon Merch or a Shopify store: one person with a folder of finished flat designs who must produce a listing image of each design on a real product, on a phone or tablet, without Photoshop and without a monthly web subscription.
paidUnit: Consumable mockup credits, which fund the generated scene and the relight that each finished mockup costs the factory to serve, plus one non-consumable unlock that removes the watermark and the free batch limit.
momentOfPayment: At the first server-cost operation after the free starter grant is spent, with the credit cost shown before the tap and the scenes the credits buy; and again at the first batch larger than the free limit, where the one-time unlock is offered beside the packs rather than in front of the first mockup.
distinctnessSentence: Warp maps a seller's own flat design file onto a product's real print area with fabric-aware warp, creases and scene lighting, and exports the listing images watermark-free on a one-time unlock, where the shelf's own leaders are measured shrinking the design into a template rectangle, holding the saved image behind a subscription, and calling an auto-renewing charge a free trial.
day1RevenuePath: A seller imports one design for free, sees it warped onto the product's true print area, buys a Starter or Studio credit pack the moment the first generated scene is worth exporting, and returns for a pack on every later design drop.
assumptionsUnverified: That a print-on-demand seller will pay for a one-time unlock and consumable credits on Android instead of a recurring web tool, which no install or conversion reading on this shelf establishes.

That the effective Play fee tier for this account stays at fifteen percent, because at twenty-five to thirty percent the floor rises to 0.0876459 to 0.0939055 dollars per credit, above every pack price proposed here.
That the recorded provider costs in the money plan still match fal prices on 2026-10-16, which only a fresh pricing read of each endpoint would settle.
That a device-side warp mesh per product reads as printed rather than pasted, which is a rendering judgement and not a measured market fact.
